item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
613
ABPZ20 KNHC 271726
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM PDT Sun Sep 27 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Polo, located southwest of Cabo San Lucas, Mexico, on recently
downgraded Tropical Storm Odalys, located well west of the southern
tip of Baja California, on Hurricane Nolo, located a few hundred
miles south-southwest of the Big Island of Hawaii, and on Tropical
Depression Eighteen-E, located several hundred miles southwest of
the Acapulco, Mexico.

Well East-Southeast of the Hawaiian Islands:
A broad area of low pressure associated with persistent showers and
thunderstorms is currently located well east-southeast of the
Hawaiian Islands. Environmental conditions are expected to be
conducive for further development, and a tropical depression is
likely to form in the next several days. The system should move
generally northeastward, and remain well east-southeast of the
Hawaiian Islands.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...medium...50 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...80 percent.

&&
Public Advisories on Tropical Depression Eighteen-E are issued under
WMO header WTPZ33 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPEP3.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Depression Eighteen-E are issued
under WMO header WTPZ23 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCMEP3.

$$
Forecaster Katz/Papin

...ODALYS QUICKLY SPINNING DOWN...
...EXPECTED TO BECOME A POST-TROPICAL CYCLONE BY TONIGHT...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 AM PDT...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...22.6N 123.4W
ABOUT 860 MI...1385 KM W OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...60 MPH...95 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...N OR 5 DEGREES AT 6 MPH...9 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...992 MB...29.30 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 AM PDT (1500 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Odalys was
located near latitude 22.6 North, longitude 123.4 West. Odalys is
moving toward the north near 6 mph (9 km/h) and a generally
northward motion is expected to continue through tonight.  By
Monday evening, Odalys should turn abruptly southward with a slight
increase in forward speed.
 
Maximum sustained winds have decreased to near 60 mph (95 km/h) 
with higher gusts.  Further rapid weakening is forecast over the 
next few days, and Odalys should degenerate to a post-tropical 
cyclone by tonight.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 105 miles (165 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 992 mb (29.30 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 PM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Roberts

item.title: Tropical Storm Odalys Forecast Discussion Number 31
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM PDT Sun Sep 27 2026 
000
WTPZ41 KNHC 271445
TCDEP1
 
Tropical Storm Odalys Discussion Number  31
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP162026
800 AM PDT Sun Sep 27 2026
 
A fortuitous 1038 UTC NOAA-20 Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer
Suite (VIIRS) Lunar calibration image indicated that Odalys is a
bit farther north than noted earlier.  The vertically shallow
tropical cyclone is quickly becoming devoid of deep convection with
a small patch located well to the northeast of the exposed surface
center.  Based on a blend of the UW-CIMSS objective techniques and
the subjective intensity estimate from TAFB, the initial intensity
is lowered to 50 kt.
 
Odalys should continue to spin down quickly while moving within an
increasingly inhibiting surrounding atmospheric environment and
over progressively cooler oceanic temperatures.  Subsequently,
Odalys is forecast to lose its deep convective organization
convection later tonight, and become a post-tropical cyclone.  On
Monday, the majority of the skilled guidance indicates that Odalys
should degenerate to a remnant low, and the NHC intensity
forecast follows suit and agrees with the various consensus aids.
 
Odalys' initial motion is estimated to be northward, or 005/5 kt.
The forecast philosophy remains unchanged, and the weakening
cyclone should continue to move generally northward in the short
term. On Monday, a severely sheared, vertically tilted Odalys
is expected to turn east-southeastward and sharply
south-southeastward while being steered by the low-level flow
produced by a subtropical high situated to the north of the cyclone.
The NHC track forecast is basically an update of the previous
advisory and lies between the HFIP HCCA and GDMI guidance.
 
Odalys' wind radii have been adjusted based on 0455 UTC METOP-C and
a 0433 UTC METOP-B scatterometer passes.
 
Distant moisture from both Hurricanes Odalys and Polo will be
transported into the southwestern United States late this weekend
and early next week, and may indirectly contribute to a heavy
rainfall and flash flood threat in the region. See products issued
by the Weather Prediction Center for more information.

item.description:
Issued at 1100 AM MST Sun Sep 27 2026 
129 
WTPZ32 KNHC 271746
TCPEP2
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Polo Intermediate Advisory Number 28A
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP172026
1100 AM MST Sun Sep 27 2026
 
...NOAA HURRICANE HUNTERS INVESTIGATING POLO...
...PREPARATIONS TO PROTECT LIFE AND PROPERTY SHOULD BE RUSHED TO
COMPLETION TODAY IN BAJA CALIFORNIA SUR AS POWERFUL POLO 
APPROACHES...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 1100 AM MST...1800 UTC...INFORMATION
-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...21.3N 114.0W
ABOUT 285 MI...460 KM WSW OF CABO SAN LUCAS MEXICO
ABOUT 265 MI...425 KM SSW OF CABO SAN LAZARO MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...125 MPH...205 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NNW OR 345 DEGREES AT 12 MPH...19 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...950 MB...28.06 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
None.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Hurricane Warning is in effect for...
* West coast of Baja California Sur, from Punta Abreojos to Santa Fe
* East coast of Baja California Sur, from Loreto to Santa Rosalia
 
A Hurricane Watch is in effect for...
* West coast of Baja California Sur, north of Punta Abreojos to
Punta Eugenia
* East coast of Baja California Sur, south of Loreto to San
Evaristo
* East coast of Baja California Sur, north of Santa Rosalia to
Bahia San Juan Bautista
* Mainland Mexico from Huatabampito to Bahia Kino
 
A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for...
* West coast of Baja California Sur, north of Punta Abreojos to
Punta Eugenia.
* East coast of Baja California Sur, north of Santa Rosalia to
Bahia San Juan Bautista
* East coast of Baja California Sur, south of Loreto to San
Evaristo.
 
A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for...
* Mainland Mexico south of Huatabampito to Topolobampo
 
A Hurricane Warning means that hurricane conditions are expected
somewhere within the warning area. A warning is typically issued
36 hours before the anticipated first occurrence of
tropical-storm-force winds, conditions that make outside
preparations difficult or dangerous. Preparations to protect life
and property should be rushed to completion.
 
A Hurricane Watch means that hurricane conditions are possible
within the watch area. A watch is typically issued 48 hours before
the anticipated first occurrence of tropical-storm-force winds,
conditions that make outside preparations difficult or dangerous.
 
A Tropical Storm Warning means that tropical storm conditions are
expected somewhere within the warning area, generally within 36
hours.
 
A Tropical Storm Watch means that tropical storm conditions are
possible within the watch area, generally within 48 hours.
 
Interests in the remainder of Baja California Sur, and the remainder
of Sonora and northern Sinaloa should monitor the progress of Polo.
 
For storm information specific to your area, please monitor
products issued by your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1100 AM MST (1800 UTC), the eye of Hurricane Polo was located by 
NOAA Hurricane Hunter aircraft near latitude 21.3 North, longitude 
114.0 West. Polo is moving toward the north-northwest near 12 mph 
(19 km/h). A turn toward the north is expected later today, followed 
by a turn toward the northeast on Monday. On the forecast track, 
Polo is expected to approach the west coast of Baja California Sur 
on Monday, move across the peninsula Monday night and then approach 
northwestern mainland Mexico by early Tuesday.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 125 mph (205 km/h) with higher 
gusts. Polo is a category 3 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson 
Hurricane Wind Scale. Fluctuations in strength are possible over the 
next day or two, but Polo is forecast to remain a strong hurricane 
when it reaches Baja California Sur on Monday.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 45 miles (75 km) from
the center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 105
miles (165 km).
 
The minimum central pressure estimated by dropsonde data is 950 mb 
(28.06 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Polo can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP2 and WMO header WTPZ42 KNHC.
 
WIND: Hurricane conditions are expected within the warning area 
along the west coast of Baja California Sur by Monday afternoon, 
with tropical storm conditions possible in the southern portion of 
the warning area by tonight into early Monday. These conditions are 
expected to spread northward and eastward across Baja California Sur 
on Monday. Hurricane conditions are possible within the Hurricane 
Watch area in mainland northwestern Mexico Monday night and Tuesday.
 
RAINFALL: Polo is expected to produce rainfall totals of 4 to 8
inches with maximum amounts of 12 inches across portions of Baja
California Sur. Rainfall totals of 4 to 6 inches with maximum totals
of 8 expected across portions of Sonora.  This rainfall may produce
life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of
steep terrain.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Polo,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep2.shtml?rainqpf
 
SURGE: A storm surge could produce significant coastal flooding in
areas of onshore winds. Near the coast, the surge will be
accompanied by large and destructive waves.
 
SURF: Swells generated by Polo will continue affecting the coast of
southwestern Mexico, west-central Mexico, and Baja California Sur
during the next couple of days. These swells will spread northward
along the coast of the Baja California Peninsula through the
remainder of the weekend. These swells are likely to cause
life-threatening surf, rip currents, and coastal flooding. Please
consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 PM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Papin

item.title: Hurricane Polo Forecast Discussion Number 28
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM MST Sun Sep 27 2026 
000
WTPZ42 KNHC 271457
TCDEP2
 
Hurricane Polo Discussion Number  28
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP172026
800 AM MST Sun Sep 27 2026
 
Polo continues to have a pretty healthy structure on geostationary
satellite imagery this morning, with very cold cloud tops associated
with robust eyewall convection. The most recent F18 SSMIS microwave
pass showed a mostly closed eyewall, albeit with some erosion on the
east side, likely due to some residual easterly vertical wind shear.
Both the subjective and objective intensity estimates over the past
6 h have increased somewhat, with the latest SATCON, DPRINT, and 
DMINT estimates between 106-113 kt. Thus, the initial intensity is 
nudged up slightly to 110 kt for this advisory. A NOAA P-3 
Hurricane Hunter aircraft is currently en route and will provide 
updated in-situ data on Polo this afternoon.
 
Polo continues to make its turn more northward, with the latest
estimated motion at 345 degrees at 10 kt. The hurricane should soon
turn northward and the northeastward over the next 12-24 h as it is
steered between the deep-layer ridging that is centered over Mexico
and a mid-latitude shortwave trough that will soon move into
California. It is this short-wave that is expected to capture Polo
as it reaches the coast of Baja California Sur, leading to further
acceleration as the hurricane turns northeastward. While the track
guidance this cycle is very tightly clustered near the previous
forecast track, but are somewhat faster along this track. Thus the
latest NHC track forecast has been moved slightly faster and
roughly splits the difference between the reliable HFIP Corrected
Consensus Approach (HCCA) and Google DeepMind ensemble mean (GDMI)
aids. Its is worth noting there remains some along-track spread in
the ensemble guidance, so the exact timing of landfall is more
uncertain than usual in the 24-48 h time frame.
 
The intensity forecast also has some challenges. Polo has maintained 
a fairly healthy appearance while its been dealing with light to 
moderate easterly vertical wind shear. The latest SHIPS guidance now 
shows the shear decreasing over the next 12-24 h, and given the 
slightly stronger initial intensity, the latest NHC intensity 
forecast is higher than the previous one. This forecast is on the 
high end of the interpolated intensity guidance, and now shows Polo 
reaching the coast of the Baja California Peninsula as a 95 kt 
hurricane. It is worth mentioning the latest HAFS-B raw model output 
shows Polo could retain major hurricane intensity at landfall. Some 
weakening should occur as it moves over the rugged terrain of Baja 
California, but it is increasingly likely that Polo's second 
landfall in mainland Mexico will also be as a (weaker) hurricane. 
Rapid weakening is forecast thereafter as it moves inland over 
Mexico with Polo becoming post-tropical or dissipating by 72 h.
 
Polo is expected to become a remnant low and then dissipate before
it reaches the southern U.S., but distant moisture associated with
it and Odalys will be transported into the southwestern United
States late this weekend and early next week, and may indirectly
contribute to a heavy rainfall and flash flood threat in the region.
See products issued by the Weather Prediction Center for more
information.
 
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Polo is forecast to approach the west coast of the Baja
California peninsula on Monday as a hurricane, and a Hurricane
Warning is in effect for that region. Tropical storm conditions
could reach portions of the coast as soon as tonight or early
Monday, making further preparations difficult. These conditions
will likely spread across Baja California through Monday. A storm
surge is likely, especially in areas of onshore winds.
 
2. Heavy rainfall associated with Polo may begin to impact Baja
California Sur tonight into Tuesday. This rainfall may produce
life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of
steep terrain.
 
3. Dangerous surf and rip currents are likely along portions of
the northwest coast of Mexico and Baja California for the next
few days.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS

 24H  28/1200Z 24.5N 113.4W  105 KT 120 MPH

item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)
item.description: ...DEPRESSION STRENGTHENS INTO A TROPICAL STORM... As of 3:00 PM CST Sun Sep 27 the center of Rachel was located near 12.6, -99.1 with movement WNW at 5 mph. The minimum central pressure was 1005 mb with maximum sustained winds of about 40 mph.

item.title: Tropical Storm Rachel Public Advisory Number 3
item.description:
Issued at 300 PM CST Sun Sep 27 2026 
000
WTPZ33 KNHC 272036
TCPEP3
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Rachel Advisory Number   3
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
300 PM CST Sun Sep 27 2026
 
...DEPRESSION STRENGTHENS INTO A TROPICAL STORM...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 300 PM CST...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...12.6N 99.1W
ABOUT 300 MI...485 KM S OF ACAPULCO MEXICO
ABOUT 560 MI...900 KM SE OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...40 MPH...65 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 290 DEGREES AT 5 MPH...7 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1005 MB...29.68 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 300 PM CST (2100 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Rachel was
located near latitude 12.6 North, longitude 99.1 West. Rachel is
moving toward the west-northwest near 5 mph (7 km/h). A faster  
west-northwest motion is expected during the next few days. On the 
forecast track, the center of Rachel is expected to remain well 
south of the coast of southern Mexico. 
 
Maximum sustained winds have increased to near 40 mph (65 km/h) 
with higher gusts. Steady strengthening is forecast during the next 
few days, and Rachel is forecast to become a hurricane on Tuesday. 
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 70 miles (110 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1005 mb (29.68 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF:  Swells generated by Rachel will begin affecting portions of 
southern coast of Mexico during the next couple of days.  These 
swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip current 
conditions.  Please consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 900 PM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Brown

item.title: Tropical Storm Rachel Forecast Discussion Number 3
item.description:
Issued at 300 PM CST Sun Sep 27 2026 
ZCZC MIATCDEP3 ALL
TTAA00 KNHC DDHHMM
 
Tropical Storm Rachel Discussion Number   3
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
300 PM CST Sun Sep 27 2026
 
Recent visible satellite imagery shows that banding features
associated the cyclone remain fragmented, but a couple of ASCAT
passes from just after 1500 UTC revealed an area of 35 kt winds to
the southeast of the center.  Therefore, the system has reached
tropical storm status, making Rachel the seventeenth named storm in 
the eastern Pacific basin this season.

Rachel is moving west-northwestward or 295/4 kt. A deep-layer 
ridge building over Mexico is expected to steer the cyclone 
west-northwest at a faster forward speed through mid-week.  This 
heading should result in the core of the storm passing well south 
of the coast of southern Mexico during the next couple of days.  
After 72 hours, a weakness is forecast to develop in the ridge 
over northwestern Mexico as a trough moves into the southwestern 
United States.  This should cause Rachel to slow, but remain on a 
northwestward to west-northwestward track when it is located well 
southwest of the coast of southwestern Mexico.  The NHC track 
forecast is similar to the previous advisory and lies close to the 
typically reliable consensus aids. 

The SHIPS model continues to diagnose about 20 kt of northeasterly 
shear over the system.  The shear does not appear to be prohibitive 
for strengthening.  In fact, most of the intensity guidance calls 
for gradual strengthening during the next couple few days, and 
Rachel is forecast to become a hurricane on Tuesday. After that 
time, there is uncertainty with regards to SSTs as Rachel may track 
over the cool wake from Hurricane Polo.  As a result, the NHC 
intensity forecast plateaus near the end of the forecast period 
between the Google Deep Mind and HFIP corrected consensus 
solutions.
